answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral, so splitting stake across keys does not dilute accountability: when k coordinated identities equivocate on conflicting messages, correlated penalties rise as O(k^2), debiting their escrows rather than treating each key independently. Detection can also trigger an exponential capital-loss multiplier across linked bonds, making a swarm costly to maintain; a vine, lantern, or walnut may be unique, but identities earn no trust without stake and evidence.
